meaning: Spot Instances are spare EC2 capacity that AWS can take back after a two-minute warning, sent on a best-effort basis. A job can run on them when losing a machine costs it little work.
The EC2 purchase option in which you pay with no commitment and AWS does not take the instance back. The instance runs until you stop it.
A robot model in which a vision-language model reads the camera images and the instruction, and an action head attached to it outputs the robot's motions.
The vision-language model that a VLA is built on. It is the part that reads the images and the text.
The part of a VLA that turns the output of the backbone into the arm's motions.
One update of a model's weights during training. Each step is computed from one batch.
One moment of a recorded episode as training reads it: the camera images and joint angles, paired with the actions that followed.
The samples that one training step processes. The per-GPU batch is what one GPU holds, and the global batch is the per-GPU batch times the number of GPUs.
For each weight that trains, the direction in which a training step moves it. It takes GPU memory alongside the weight.
The running statistics that the optimiser keeps from step to step for each weight that trains. A frozen weight has no optimiser state.
The intermediate values that the forward pass computes for each sample. They stay in GPU memory until the backward pass uses them, so they grow with the batch.
A training setting that recomputes the activations during the backward pass instead of storing them. It trades extra compute for less GPU memory.
Describes weights that training reads but does not update. Frozen weights need no gradient and no optimiser state.
Further training that updates every weight of a pretrained model.
The published configuration of a training run. It sets the model, the batch size, the number of steps and which weights train.
A fine-tuning method that freezes the original weights and trains small extra matrices added next to them. It cuts the memory that a fine-tune needs.
A fine-tuning setting that leaves the vision-language model unchanged and trains only the action head and the layer that feeds it.
The part of the backbone that turns camera images into vectors.
A way to train on several GPUs. Each GPU keeps a copy of the model and works through its own share of the batch, and the GPUs combine their gradients into one update per step.

A form of data-parallel training that splits the weights, gradients and optimiser state across the GPUs instead of keeping a full copy on each. You use it when the training state of a model does not fit on one GPU.
The number of GPUs a job uses multiplied by the hours it uses them. It measures GPU time, not work, because GPU models differ in speed.
The first training of a model, on data from many robots or on video, before the model has seen your robot.
Any training that starts from a pretrained checkpoint. Its size ranges from one GPU to several servers.
A saved copy of a model's weights. During a run, it also means the saved state that the run can resume from after a stop.
One pass of training over every frame of the dataset.
One server in a training job, such as an EC2 instance with eight GPUs.
A CPU process that reads and decodes samples and prepares them into batches for the GPU.
EC2's unit of processor capacity, equal to one hardware thread. Most eight-GPU instance sizes come with 24 vCPUs per GPU.
A 2-byte number format for model weights. NVIDIA lists GR00T N1.7 in this format.
A small policy of about 80M parameters that predicts a chunk of actions at a time. It is trained from scratch on one task.
Training in which the policy improves from scored attempts. In this section, the attempts run in a simulator.
Meta's action-conditioned model that predicts how a scene changes when the arm acts. Meta trained it on top of its V-JEPA 2 video encoder, on under 62 hours of robot video, with the encoder frozen.
A SageMaker service that starts instances for one training job and shuts them down when the job ends.
The SageMaker Training Jobs setting that runs a job on Spot Instances. It copies the job's checkpoints to S3 and back, and resumes the job after an interruption. It does not fall back to On-Demand.
AWS's persistent training cluster. By default, it deploys a cluster in one Availability Zone.
AWS's managed Lustre file system, which many processes can read in parallel. It is used to keep data and checkpoints between training jobs.
AWS's managed Kubernetes service. Its best-practices guide gives the checkpoint intervals cited in this section.
The EC2 network device for traffic between instances. It bypasses the operating system kernel so that many machines can train as one. The small GPU instance sizes do not have it.
One of the separate groups of data centres inside an AWS Region. EFA traffic cannot cross from one Availability Zone to another.
An EC2 setting that packs instances close together on the network. AWS Batch requires one for EFA jobs.
A SageMaker HyperPod feature, built on NVIDIA NeMo, that rebuilds a failed node's training state from its healthy peers instead of restarting from a saved checkpoint.
A HyperPod feature for PyTorch on EKS. It keeps checkpoints in the nodes' CPU memory, copies them to adjacent nodes, and periodically saves them to durable storage such as S3.
Large simulation and scientific jobs that run across many servers, which exchange data while they compute. AWS's HPC team tested such a job on Spot Instances.
An open-source job scheduler for clusters. AWS's HPC test on Spot Instances ran under Slurm.
NVIDIA's training framework. HyperPod's checkpointless training is built on it.
An EC2 reservation of P or Trainium instances for a set period. No G-family instances are offered.
A SageMaker reservation of P or Trainium capacity for 1 to 182 days, which you can book up to 8 weeks ahead.
